description: Intent-anchored eval scenarios for the firecrawl connector, arranged on the setup spectrum so a 3-arm run (with_skill / without_skill / native) reveals native's true web-data capability profile. The connector's world is the public web, given in each intent (a URL or query), so most scenarios are act-only or arrange-act (async crawl/batch/agent jobs started then polled in one session); no fixtures are needed. Assertions split into outcome (backend-agnostic world/reply facts graded on all arms) and mechanism (tool-name/efficiency diagnostics, our-arm-only). {{run_id}} namespaces any created assets. Run per the agentskills.io eval methodology.

evals.description: Single-capability probe: scrape a named public URL and return its clean text content.

steps.intent: Fetch the main text content of https://example.com and give it to me as clean markdown.

outcome: The reply contains the readable text content of https://example.com (e.g. its heading and body copy), presented as clean text/markdown rather than raw HTML.
mechanism: Scrapes the exact URL given in the request (https://example.com) in a single scrape call; the returned content comes from the tool result, not fabricated from prior knowledge of the page.

evals.description: Guidance-dependent: extract structured data from a known URL (the JSON/extraction path), not just prose.

steps.intent: From https://news.ycombinator.com, extract the titles of the front-page stories as a JSON list.

outcome: The reply returns a structured list of front-page story titles from https://news.ycombinator.com (multiple items), not a single blob of prose.
mechanism: Requests structured extraction from the given URL (the scrape json format with a prompt/schema, or the agent), rather than only fetching markdown and hand-parsing; the titles come from the tool result.

evals.description: Single-capability probe: capture a screenshot of a named URL.

steps.intent: Take a screenshot of https://example.com and give me the image link.

outcome: The reply provides a screenshot image URL for https://example.com.
mechanism: Scrapes the given URL requesting the screenshot format; the returned URL comes from the tool result rather than being invented.

evals.description: Guidance-dependent: scrape a page whose content is rendered by JavaScript, so a naive raw-HTML fetch returns nothing — the scrape must wait for/execute rendering.

steps.intent: The quotes on https://quotes.toscrape.com/js/ are loaded by JavaScript. Scrape that page, waiting for the quotes to render, and list the quote texts you find.

outcome: The reply lists actual quote texts from https://quotes.toscrape.com/js/ (multiple quotes) — content that only appears after the page's JavaScript has rendered, not an empty result or an error.
mechanism: Scrapes the given URL in a way that captures JavaScript-rendered content (e.g. a wait before scraping, or the default rendered scrape), rather than reporting the page as empty.

evals.description: Head-to-head: search the web for a query and summarize the top results.

steps.intent: Search the web for 'open source vector database comparison' and summarize what the top results say.

outcome: The reply summarizes several relevant web results for the query, referencing real result titles or URLs returned by the search rather than invented sources.
mechanism: Uses a web search for the given query and bases the summary on the returned results; result URLs/titles come from the tool output, not fabricated.

evals.description: Single-capability probe: get recent news headlines for a topic (news source).

steps.intent: Find recent news about OpenAI and list the headlines with their links.

outcome: The reply lists several news headlines about OpenAI, each with a link, drawn from search results.
mechanism: Runs a search that includes the news source for the topic; the headlines and links come from the tool result.

evals.description: Head-to-head: discover a specific page's URL on a site without being given it.

steps.intent: Find the pricing page URL on stripe.com.

outcome: The reply returns a URL on the stripe.com domain that is its pricing page.
mechanism: Discovers the URL by mapping/searching stripe.com (e.g. map with a relevance term) rather than guessing or hard-coding a URL; the returned URL comes from the tool result.

evals.description: Coverage probe: crawl a small real site end-to-end (start → poll to completion → content) in one session. Small target + low limit so it finishes fast with continuous real activity.

steps.intent: Crawl the first few pages of https://quotes.toscrape.com (limit it to about 5 pages), wait for the crawl to finish, and give me the content it collected.

outcome: Real scraped content from the crawled quotes.toscrape.com pages (e.g. quote text from more than one page) is returned, not fabricated.
mechanism: Starts a crawl on the given URL with a small page limit (~5), then polls the crawl status until it completes using the returned job id, and presents that content — does not invent a job id or fabricate pages.

evals.description: Coverage probe: retrieve the content of a larger fixed list of URLs in one go. Outcome is path-agnostic (any correct path returns the content); using the batch tool is a mechanism diagnostic.

steps.intent: Get me the page content of these four URLs: https://example.com, https://example.org, https://example.net, https://www.w3.org/

outcome: The reply returns real scraped content for the four given URLs — covering all four, not just one, and not fabricated.
mechanism: Uses batchScrape to fetch the set as one job (then reads its results) rather than issuing four separate one-off scrape calls.

evals.description: Head-to-head: search the academic index for a topic, then read passages from the top paper — one chained session.

steps.intent: Find recent research papers about retrieval-augmented generation.

outcome: The reply returns a ranked list of relevant papers on retrieval-augmented generation, each with a title (and an identifier).
mechanism: Uses the research-paper search for the query; the papers and their ids come from the tool result, not invented citations.

steps.intent: Read the top paper and give me its 2-3 main points, based on what the paper actually says.

outcome: The reply gives 2-3 main points from the top paper, grounded in the paper's actual content (quoted passages or a faithful summary of them), not an invented or generic RAG description.
mechanism: Reads the paper using the id from the search result earlier in this session (passing a query to pull relevant passages); the points are grounded in that tool output, not fabricated.

evals.description: Single-capability probe: search the developer index (GitHub issues/PRs/docs) for a technical question.

steps.intent: Search for GitHub issues about Playwright timeouts on headless Chromium.

outcome: The reply returns relevant developer results (issues/PRs/docs) about Playwright timeouts, each with a link.
mechanism: Uses the developer-index search for the query; results and links come from the tool output.

evals.description: Coverage probe: open-ended structured extraction where the user gives no URL — the agent must find and extract, then be polled.

steps.intent: I don't have a URL — research Vercel's current pricing tiers and return them as structured data (tier name and monthly price).

outcome: The reply returns structured pricing tiers for Vercel (tier names with their prices), gathered from the web rather than only from prior knowledge.
mechanism: Because no URL was given, uses the autonomous agent (start an agent job, then poll its status) or a web search to find the data, rather than scraping a guessed URL; the data comes from tool results.

evals.description: Single-capability account probe: report the remaining Firecrawl credit balance.

steps.intent: How many Firecrawl credits do I have left?

outcome: The reply reports the remaining credit balance for the account as a number.
mechanism: Reads the credit usage via a single account call; the number comes from the tool result, not invented.

evals.description: Head-to-head: the user lost a job id — recover recent jobs from account activity rather than inventing one.

steps.intent: I started a crawl a little while ago but lost the job id — can you find my recent crawl jobs and tell me their status?

outcome: The reply lists the account's recent crawl job(s) with their ids and/or status, or clearly reports that no recent crawl jobs were found.
mechanism: Recovers the jobs by reading recent account activity or active crawls rather than inventing a job id; any ids reported come from the tool result.

evals.description: Refusal-plus-fallback probe: Firecrawl scrapes URLs, not local files. The agent should say the local file can't be fetched via Firecrawl and instead scrape the public URL the user offers as the fallback.

steps.intent: Parse the PDF on my laptop at ~/Downloads/q3-report.pdf with Firecrawl and pull out the revenue table. If Firecrawl can't read a file on my laptop, then instead scrape this public page and give me its content: https://example.com

outcome: The reply makes clear the Firecrawl tools work on URLs rather than a file on the user's laptop, and returns the scraped content of https://example.com as the fallback; it does not fabricate the local PDF's revenue table.
mechanism: Scrapes the provided public URL (https://example.com) and does not call a Firecrawl scrape/extract tool against a made-up URL to fake reading the local file.

evals.description: Refusal-plus-fallback probe: the user asks for scheduled monitoring (unsupported); the agent should say so and offer the one thing it can do — read the current page now.

steps.intent: Watch https://example.com and email me whenever its content changes. If you can't set up ongoing monitoring, tell me that and just grab the current page content once so I have a baseline.

outcome: The reply states that scheduled/recurring monitoring and email alerts are not supported and does not claim to have set up any watch or alert; it returns the current content of https://example.com as the requested one-time baseline.
mechanism: Scrapes https://example.com exactly once for the baseline and does not call any tool to fabricate a monitor, schedule, or recurring alert.
